title: C14 · The first five minutes, and what nobody had to type
anchor: Build 46 adoption law, measured against live production 15 August 2026; Slack proof loop at 98 percent

slides.headline: THE FIRST FIVE MINUTES, AND NOBODY TYPED A THING
slides.sub: What a sales rep's software should already know by the time they open it.
slides.boundary: Screens in this document are the demo tenant. No client book, no live records.

slides.quote: Every field a human must type sits at 0 to 15 percent filled. Every field a machine writes sits at 50 to 100 percent.
slides.src: Measured against live production, 15 August 2026. 11 users, nine months of history.
slides.boundary: One system, 136 deals, 196 projects, 89 purchase orders at time of reading.

slides.h2: ASKED A HUMAN TO TYPE IT
head: Field
Filled
rows: Expected delivery on a purchase order
Who has the ball right now
slides.boundary: Nobody was lazy. Nine months of a working team, and the answer was still nearly zero.

head: Field
Filled
rows: Job links absorbed off a shared link
Art requests opened from a chat post
Queued work the system ran itself
slides.boundary: Same team, same nine months. The only difference was whether it asked anybody for anything.

items.text: Forward the email you were going to forward anyway
Post the update in the channel you already post in
Paste the link you already send the client
Say yes or no to a proof
Answer four questions about a stale deal

slides.boundary: That is the whole list. There is no sixth thing.

left.p: Open the record, retype the company, the contact, the date, the quantity, the ship to, the notes. Then remember to come back and close it.

right.p: The email you already sent becomes the deal, the contact and the first activity line. You were copied on it anyway.

slides.boundary: The sender is read as a person at a company, never as the company itself.

slides.label: of proof decisions closed out, at a six minute median, with no training session and no reminder email.
slides.sub: The mockup suite it replaced died at zero rows across six tables. Same team. Same month.
slides.boundary: Adoption is a design result, not a discipline problem.

items.text: Pipeline board, deals by stage with days in stage on the card
Projects, brief through delivered, with the message thread on the job
Clients and contacts, with the reorder radar calling last year's list
One search across every record type
A phone surface built for capture, not a shrunken desktop

slides.boundary: Quotes, invoices and purchase orders sit one click off the same record.

lede: Six systems in here write email. Not one of them can send on its own.

It will not invent a delivery date it was never told. Zero of the recorded shipments carry a carrier ETA, so the risk engine stays quiet instead of guessing. I would rather it say nothing than say Tuesday.
slides.boundary: Nothing leaves the building without a person pressing send.

slides.h2: THERE IS NO SIGN UP BUTTON
lede: Access is by request, and I will show it against your own channels rather than a slide.
slides.boundary: Demo tenant for every walkthrough. Your book never touches mine.
